title: The Concept of Social Capital
text:
Social capital refers to the aggregate of the actual or potential resources linked to possession of a durable network of relationships. These resources are not tangible assets but rather the value derived from social connections, such as trust and reciprocity within a community.

The formation of social capital is heavily dependent on group membership and institutional structures. It often acts as an accelerant for collective action, allowing groups to mobilize resources more effectively than individuals acting in isolation. Stronger community ties generally correlate with higher levels of economic stability and civic engagement.

Different forms of social capital—such as bonding (ties within homogeneous groups) versus bridging (ties between diverse groups)—have varying implications for social cohesion and overall societal resilience.
